clue.text: Skilled performer taking on part that is his greatest achievement

parts.note: a master is an expert craftsman or performer
a piece is a part or portion of something

explanation.surface: An actor accepts a role that turns out to be the crowning glory of his career.
explanation.definitionFit: A masterpiece is the finest work an artist ever produces.

clue.text: A bar erected on quarter deck

indicators.note: erected means set upright, and in a down clue that makes the bar read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rod is a bar of metal or wood
N for north is one of the four quarters or cardinal points of the compass

explanation.surface: A rail has been put up on part of a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' looks like a ship's floor, but here it is the verb meaning to decorate. 'erected' turns ROD into DOR.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck something is to adorn or decorate it, as with holly.

clue.text: Reconstruction of Capitol of interest today

indicators.note: a reconstruction rebuilds the word Capitol from its letters in a new order

explanation.surface: The rebuilding of the Washington Capitol is a newsworthy matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A current-affairs subject is relevant to present events.

clue.text: Revolutionary gutter press that invites getting tossed aside?

parts.note: red is the colour associated with communist revolutionaries
a rag is a disreputable newspaper, part of the gutter press

explanation.surface: A radical tabloid newspaper that deserves to be thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the idiom 'like a red rag to a bull': waving one provokes the bull, inviting it to toss you aside on its horns.
explanation.definitionFit: Provocation that enrages a bull is the classic image here, the bull tossing the waver.

clue.text: Some hesitation to point out odd Latin where the heart is concerned

indicators.note: the rearranged Latin lies out, around the outside of the other letters
odd says the letters of Latin are unusual, so rearranged

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
N for north is a compass point

explanation.surface: A hesitant attempt to note a strange Latin phrase about emotional matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges LATIN into INTAL, and 'out' places it outside ER + N (er then point), giving INT-ERN-AL.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart is inside the body, so it concerns the inner organs.

clue.text: Nestling saying "Cheer up

parts.note: a young bird's chirp sounds like someone saying the words cheer up

explanation.walkthrough: The bird's chirping noise sounds like 'cheer up' said quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: A short shrill chirp is the twittering call of a small bird.

clue.text: Freedom expected from roll on a section where traffic coud meet head-on

definitions.text: a section where traffic coud meet head-on

explanation.surface: A road safety note about stretches of highway with oncoming vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coud' is a misprint of 'could'. A roll-on is an elasticated girdle rolled on rather than laced; its fabric gives in both directions. A road where cars travel both ways is a stretch of the second kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic fabric giving in both directions, and a length of road carrying opposing traffic, share this name.

clue.text: Violet and I slipped into gallery, day having been spoiled

parts.note: Vi is the short form of the name Violet

indicators.note: slipped into means the letter I is placed inside the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is a famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: Violet and I sneaked into an art gallery, and the day was ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: THE TATE is a group of national art galleries in Britain. I goes inside TATE to make TIATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vitiated has been impaired, its quality corrupted.

clue.text: Broadly speaking like Monty's style?

explanation.surface: Speaking loosely, the way Montgomery did things.
explanation.walkthrough: Monty is Field Marshal Montgomery, the British general of the Second World War, so his manner was that of a general.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means roughly or on the whole, and read literally it is the manner of a military commander.

clue.text: Who operates in the case of a cough symptom?

parts.note: OP is the short form of operation or operates, as in a surgical op; that the two words also run on unbroken is a coincidence of the charade, not a hidden word

explanation.surface: A question about which doctor performs surgery on someone with a cough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the case of' is a link. The cough is whooping cough, whose sufferers draw breath with a whooping noise.
explanation.definitionFit: The noisy intake of breath in whooping cough is called the whoop.

clue.text: Worn away and tired out when it is turned on

definitions.note: the clue gives an adjective phrase, the entry is the noun for the wearing away itself

indicators.note: tired out suggests exhaustion, but out signals that the letters of tired are rearranged
is turned tells us the little word it is flipped round to read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone exhausted perks up the moment a device is switched on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns TIRED into DETRI; 'is turned' makes IT read TI; ON follows, so DETRI + TI + ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Detrition is the process of rubbing or wearing something down by friction.

clue.text: Just the seat for the sky pilot's relaxation?

definitions.text: Just the seat for the sky pilot's relaxation?

parts.words: Just the seat for the sky pilot's relaxation?
parts.note: a sky pilot is slang for a chaplain, but read literally as an airman, he would relax in an armchair named after part of an aircraft

explanation.surface: A recommendation of a comfortable chair for a clergyman to unwind in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sky pilot' is old slang for a chaplain or padre; the clue reads it as a literal flyer, whose aircraft has wings.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a high-backed armchair with side pieces projecting at head height.

clue.text: Organised rugger men given bad gin and feeling sorry for it

parts.note: RU stands for Rugby Union, the organised body of rugby players

indicators.note: bad gin is spoilt, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rugby players handed poor-quality spirits come to regret drinking them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges GIN into ING, which follows RU.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to regret it, so this is regretting.

clue.text: Elf and fay brought back a green bird

indicators.note: brought back says the two words elf and fay, taken together, are read in reverse order

explanation.surface: Two fairy creatures return home with a green-feathered bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' reverses ELFFAY in full, giving the bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The yaffle is a country name for the green woodpecker, from its laughing call.

clue.text: Prairie dwellers having no obstacles in competing

explanation.surface: Plains-dwelling peoples compete without hurdles.
explanation.walkthrough: A prairie is level, so its people are a people of the plains; a horse race without jumps is the other sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of people on level ground, and a horse race run without fences, share the phrase.

clue.text: But recognised artists inserted a very badly-painted Russian

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist recognised by the Royal Academy, so RAs are several of them
something inserted has been put in

explanation.surface: Officially honoured painters have hung a portrait of a Russian that is dreadfully done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'But' is a link. 'Painted' means portrayed: the mystic adviser to the last Tsar is usually shown as a villain, so he is badly painted in reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: Grigori Rasputin, the Russian mystic at the Romanov court, is remembered with a notoriously black reputation.

clue.text: Nothing little Minnie does takes in men at masked balls

indicators.note: takes in means the word does swallows the other letters inside it

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, means nothing
Min is the short form of the name Minnie

explanation.surface: Little Minnie doesn't do much, but she welcomes men to masquerade dances.
explanation.walkthrough: O and MIN go inside DOES between the D and the OES.
explanation.definitionFit: A domino is a hooded cloak with a half-mask, and by extension the person wearing one at a masquerade.

clue.text: Pathetically small waterfall

parts.note: a tiny fall of water shed out of pathos, from the eye rather than over a cliff

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pathetically' reads as 'feebly' but means 'out of pathos': it is a single drop of sadness falling down a cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: A single drop shed from the eye in sorrow is the smallest possible fall of water.

clue.text: Sober country sought by the sailor?

parts.note: dry means not drinking alcohol, so sober
land is a country or nation

explanation.surface: A teetotal nation that a mariner sets out to find.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is the sailor wanting terra firma after time at sea, not a drink-free country.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaman at sea longs for terra firma, ground that is not water.

clue.text: A successful one wants a lot more than his rivals

definitions.text: A successful one wants a lot more than his rivals

parts.words: A successful one wants a lot more than his rivals
parts.note: at an auction, the person who makes the winning offer is the one who wanted that lot more keenly than the others in the room

explanation.surface: An ambitious person is greedier than any of his competitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' looks like 'much', but a lot is an item put up at auction.
explanation.definitionFit: At an auction, whoever offers money for a lot is making a bid.

clue.text: Such emotions are strained in teens

definitions.note: the clue gives a clause; the entry is the adjective describing such feelings

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: strained suggests stress, but signals that the letters of in and teens are wrenched into a new order

explanation.surface: Feelings run high and tight among teenagers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strained' rearranges TEENS into TENSE, which follows IN; the surface reads it as tension in teenagers.
explanation.definitionFit: Feelings that are extreme and deeply felt are strong or passionate.

clue.text: Ask for more depth from river writer

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales
a pen is an instrument for writing

explanation.surface: Someone requests more detail from an author who lives by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link. The definition is the imperative: telling someone to make a hole bigger asks for more depth.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something go further down is to increase how far it reaches.

clue.text: Like a nobleman before his time?

explanation.surface: A peer who arrives ahead of schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as EARL-Y, the word looks like an adjective formed from a peer's title, as 'manly' comes from man.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British nobleman, and the word also means ahead of the appointed hour.

clue.text: There are no differences among idle characters I can't sort out

definitions.note: the clue gives a clause, the entry is the adjective describing things with no differences

indicators.note: to sort out letters is to put them into a new order, which marks an anagram

explanation.surface: Someone lazy admits that they cannot get their affairs in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' is a link: the letters of IDLE, I and CANT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that match exactly in every detail show no variation at all.

clue.text: A Somerset town said to be badly affected by fire

indicators.note: said to be signals that the word for burnt is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: something burnt and blackened by fire is charred

explanation.surface: A West Country town reportedly suffered a serious blaze.
explanation.walkthrough: Chard is a market town in Somerset, a county in south-west England; it sounds like the word for scorched.
explanation.definitionFit: Chard is a small market town in the south-west English county of Somerset.

clue.text: Put a ring on a rooster or the reverse with a feeling of triumph

indicators.note: the clue first puts the ring on the bird, then says the reverse order is wanted, so the bird comes first

parts.note: a cock is a male chicken, a rooster
taken as written
a hoop is a circular band, a ring

explanation.surface: Instructions for banding a farmyard bird, delivered with great glee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put a ring on a rooster' would give the ring first; 'or the reverse' puts the bird first, then A, then the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Being exultant or crowing over a success is the sense of this old phrase.

clue.text: The old Malawi, as any new order shows

indicators.note: a new order of letters is a rearrangement of the words as and any

explanation.surface: A remark that a fresh regime in a former African country reveals its old name.
explanation.walkthrough: Malawi in east Africa was once the British protectorate of Nyasaland, and Lake Malawi was called Lake Nyasa.
explanation.definitionFit: Before independence the territory, and its great lake, were named after this former name.

clue.text: Scraps over remnants

explanation.surface: Bits and pieces left over after a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe miscellaneous leftover bits and pieces, which this phrase names.
